title: Khala Privacy — Research and Claim Audit
scope: All 23 slides reviewed for claim wording, labels, numerical consistency and evidence provenance. Targeted primary-source verification covers slide 15 and UR (SN25) mechanism/launch wording. This is not a complete fresh fact-check of every financial metric, legal date or product claim.

slide_15.paper: Time Tells All: Deanonymization of Blockchain RPC Users with Zero Transaction Fee (Extended Version)
slide_15.scope: Links IPs to wallet pseudonyms/addresses from traffic timing under a strong passive observer. Researchers used controlled endpoints and emulated routers, not an actual ISP deployment. Three or four observations and frequency-filter assumptions matter. Not population-wide exposure or named-person identification.
slide_15.limits: Dynamic IPs, NAT, missing observations and network conditions can reduce success. Tor/VPN defenses are not resolved by the study; UR (SN25) was not tested. This is a preprint result, not an independent replication.
slide_15.cve: The prior slide mentioned a CVE. That claim was removed from the tooltip because this audit did not independently establish the registry record.

issues.Issue: CORRECTED: “95–98% of wallet traffic” used the wrong denominator and omitted the strong observer setup. The study reports address-linking success in controlled experiments, not the share of all users exposed or identification of named people.
issues.Recommended fix: Keep the corrected subtitle and visible experimental-scope qualification. Do not imply that UR (SN25) was tested or proven to prevent the attack.

issues.Issue: OPEN — PUBLICATION HOLD: the monthly bars are sample data. The 350K headline, 126,717 providers and 103 countries are supplied/team-reported, not independently substantiated in this audit.
issues.Recommended fix: Retain the requested placeholder in this review draft. Replace it with dated, defined and evidenced observations before public/client release.

issues.Issue: OPEN: the critical proving-vulnerability assertion, v6 remediation, 200,000 staking threshold, 20% governance mint cap and November unlock are not primary-source verified in this audit. These can materially change the investment story.
issues.Recommended fix: Obtain exact official disclosure, protocol/tokenomics and unlock references before external reliance. Remove or qualify any unsupported assertion.

issues.Issue: CORRECTED: 96.8% was labelled “Ethereum, MetaMask” and described as a real-world experiment without identifying the testnet.
issues.Recommended fix: Keep separate Ethereum mainnet (95.33%) and testnet (96.80%) rows, with MetaMask and three observations. Bitcoin/Electrum and Solana/Torus are testnet experiments with four observations.

issues.Issue: CORRECTED: “independently measure” was inconsistent with the official launch documentation, which describes a UR-run operator and sole validator.
issues.Recommended fix: Retain the launch qualification; describe independent validation as a design goal/assumption rather than an established launch property.

issues.Issue: CORRECTED: approximately 200 fleets read as an observed count; it is a design capacity. The diagram’s standard emission allocation was not distinguished from launch provider allocation.
issues.Recommended fix: Keep “Up to 200” and the design-capacity label. Keep the visible distinction between mechanism design and documented launch allocation.

issues.Issue: CORRECTED: the text equated deposits with required new market buying. Official documentation says revenue-funded purchases are expected off-chain, not enforced.
issues.Recommended fix: Describe token locking separately from net market purchases. Keep scenarios conditional on pricing, traffic and funding assumptions.

issues.Issue: CORRECTED: speculative spending of the existing reserve conflicted with the one-way reserve design.
issues.Recommended fix: State that the current reserve has no outbound transfer path. A future different architecture is not an existing holder right.

issues.Issue: OPEN: supplied snapshots, company metrics, fees, revenue, fund-raising and peer values are not a fresh independently verified dataset. Broad publisher names are insufficient to reproduce each observation.
issues.Recommended fix: Attach exact source URLs, observation dates, metric definitions and archived data extracts in the evidence register. Preserve the 15 October snapshot until the entire comparison is refreshed consistently.

issues.Issue: OPEN: future court dates, unlock dates, product launches and roadmap status are retained from supplied research; this audit did not independently confirm them.
issues.Recommended fix: Verify each against the official docket, announcement or release. Mark plans as conditional and date the status.

issues.Issue: OPEN: device encryption, server retention, issuance reduction, DIEM economics and buyback rate remain supplied claims with secondary attributions.
issues.Recommended fix: Check official product architecture, privacy policy and tokenomics. Do not conflate encrypted transport or non-retention with end-to-end confidential inference.

issues.Issue: PARTLY CORRECTED: the refund example is now explicitly historical (2025). The official roadmap supports a planned linkability mitigation, not confirmation of its current rollout. The $1.5B figure remains supplied sponsored research.
issues.Recommended fix: Confirm the original incident and current implementation separately. Keep sponsored-research attribution for the volume claim and do not present the historical example as a newly tested current flaw.

issues.Issue: CORRECTED: the graphic could imply a calibrated crossover where operator buying exceeds emissions. No model or deposit rate was supplied.
issues.Recommended fix: Keep the explicit illustrative/no-calibration statement and avoid using the crossover as a quantitative forecast.

issues.Issue: OPEN ASSUMPTION: bear/base/bull ranges have no supplied cash-flow or deposit-based valuation model.
issues.Recommended fix: Keep “illustrative assumptions” visible and in machine-readable outputs; supply assumptions and sensitivity analysis before treating ranges as targets.

issues.Issue: OPEN INTERPRETATION: the chart cannot establish that token value capture caused different peer valuations. Market caps differ in supply, business models and risk.
issues.Recommended fix: Treat the comparison as context, not causal proof. The 10× and 58× calculations are arithmetic comparisons, not expected returns.

issues.Issue: CORRECTED: mixed UR, SN25 and SN25 UR labels made the project reference inconsistent.
issues.Recommended fix: Use UR (SN25) for the project. Keep the distinct URnetwork product name and technical IDs/URLs unchanged.
Keep rounded wording around 1,000×, 10× and 58×; retain the snapshot date and illustrative qualification.

coverage.title: Privacy products are growing, but token value capture remains uneven
coverage.finding: Summary checked against displayed claims; evidence for supplied adoption, market values and milestones remains open.

coverage.title: Privacy is becoming necessary for corporate payments
coverage.finding: Story divider; no new quantitative assertion. Corporate confidentiality is a thesis rather than independently established universal necessity.

coverage.title: Public ledgers expose the activity behind $306B of stablecoins
coverage.finding: Snapshot units and hierarchy checked; stablecoin totals, issuer share and quote require exact dated primary references.

coverage.title: Buterin and Durov both place privacy in core infrastructure
coverage.finding: Founder positions and the Cloud Chat/Secret Chat distinction retained; quote provenance and user count were not independently re-verified.

coverage.title: US policy has shifted toward privacy, while developer liability remains open
coverage.finding: Policy timeline retained; exact legal event dates and their scope remain primary-source verification tasks.

coverage.title: Payroll and trading are the first commercial tests of confidentiality
coverage.finding: Deployments remain company-reported; network-level correlation is supported by the study only under its stated setup.

coverage.title: Privacy demand alone does not set token value
coverage.finding: Nym plus UR (SN25) only in the network-privacy subset; total recomputed. Peer figures and valuation causality remain unverified.

coverage.title: Token designs differ in how usage reaches holders
coverage.finding: Story divider; no new numerical claim.

coverage.title: Privacy tokens capture value differently
coverage.finding: Project naming and non-comparable adoption-metric qualification checked; individual product/token claims remain supplied research.

coverage.title: Zcash prices in future private use
coverage.finding: Chart and prose use supplied Zcash history and fees; sponsored research attribution retained; no independent refresh.

coverage.title: Aztec has $12M staked against $58K in user funds
coverage.finding: Critical disclosure, staking, minting and unlock claims need exact primary sources before external reliance.

coverage.title: Umbra’s fees reach its treasury, with no automatic payout to holders
coverage.finding: Treasury/holder distinction and supplied conditional vesting retained; primary tokenomics and adoption proof remain open.

coverage.title: Venice converts part of customer revenue into VVV buybacks
coverage.finding: Product privacy, tokenomics and financial claims require official architecture and economics evidence.

coverage.title: UR (SN25) has users, but priced deposits have yet to begin
coverage.finding: Naming corrected; deposit pricing is conditional. Established audience figures remain team-reported.

coverage.title: Wallet privacy can fail at network connections and cross-chain swaps
coverage.finding: Primary TRAP paper checked; mainnet/testnet labels, unit of success, observation count and scope corrected. Historical swap case separated from current status.

coverage.title: UR (SN25) reports 350K monthly users
coverage.finding: Sample monthly series preserved at user request with NOT FOR POSTING label; no claim that sample bars are observed history.

coverage.title: UR (SN25) uses validator scores to reward routing capacity
coverage.finding: Official mechanism and validator documentation checked; independence, fleet capacity and launch/design distinction corrected. Team metrics not independently verified.

coverage.title: Priced deposits could create demand for UR (SN25)
coverage.finding: Token locking separated from new purchases; threshold explicitly illustrative; zero-rate launch distinguished from conditional priced deposits.

coverage.title: UR (SN25) would be worth 10× at Helium’s market cap and 58× at Grass’s
coverage.finding: 10×/58× arithmetic checked from supplied inputs; deposit wording corrected. No price target or causal valuation proof.

coverage.title: Operator deposits could link UR (SN25) demand to usage
coverage.finding: One-way reserve and deposit-funding copy corrected. Precise Bittensor emission-lookback description remains a verification task.

coverage.title: UR (SN25)’s operator roadmap extends from consumer VPNs into enterprise and AI
coverage.finding: Research projects remain labelled; peer scale is not UR (SN25) revenue. Roadmap/admission status and addressable-market inputs need dated primary evidence.

coverage.title: Operator deposits distinguish the illustrative UR (SN25) scenarios
coverage.finding: Scenarios remain assumptions with no supplied valuation model; nothing in this audit certifies end-2027 outcomes.

coverage.title: Dated events and operating signals will test the privacy thesis
coverage.finding: Calendar combines scheduled, conditional and recurring indicators; all material future dates require official confirmation.

verdict: Return for rework before public/client release: sample data and unresolved material evidence remain.
priorities: Replace slide 16 sample series with verified, defined observations before publication.
Obtain primary disclosure and tokenomics evidence for slide 11.
Complete exact-source evidence for material market, adoption, revenue and future-date claims.
Keep the corrected study limitations, launch-state distinctions and conditional purchase/deposit wording.
Preserve the approved design and synchronize every export and machine-readable format.

validation.automated: 23-slide source/export text and geometry parity, links and downloads, byline and desktop/mobile modal DOM passed.
validation.browser: Live browser checked: slide 15 caveats visible within the grid, slide 17 KPI text within boxes, renamed comparison labels within the grid; light/dark checks reported separately.
